source.text: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ עַל־שׁוּשַׁ֣ן עֵד֑וּת מִכְתָּ֖ם לְדָוִ֣ד לְלַמֵּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director, on Shushan Eduth, a miktam of David, to teach,

en.L: For the director: on shushan eduth. A miktam of David, for teaching,
en.B: For the music director. On shushan eduth. A miktam of David, for teaching,
en.R: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Lily of the Covenant." A song of David, to be taught.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : sur shoushan édouth. Un miktam de David, pour enseigner,
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Sur shoushan édouth. Un miktam de David, pour l’enseignement,
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Sur l’air « Le lis de l’alliance ». Un chant de David, à enseigner.

sw.L: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: juu ya shushani edothi. Mikitamu ya Daudi, kwa ajili ya kufundisha,
sw.B: Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Juu ya shushani edothi. Mikitamu ya Daudi, kwa ajili ya kufundisha,
sw.R: Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Kwa sauti ya wimbo "Yungiyungi wa Agano." Wimbo wa Daudi, wa kufundishwa.

es.L: Al director del coro: sobre susán edut. Un mictam de David, para enseñar,
es.B: Al director del coro. Sobre susán edut. Un mictam de David, para enseñar,
es.R: Para el director de la música. Con la melodía «El lirio del pacto». Un canto de David, para que se enseñe.

decisions.choice: The title is verses 1-2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts this long title as two verses, so the verse numbers here are two higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: on shushan eduth: "on the lily of the testimony"
alternatives: to the tune of a song called Lily of the Covenant
decisions.reason: The words mean "lily" and "testimony" (the terms of God's covenant, 19:8). They probably name a tune or a way of singing; compare "on shoshannim" in 45:1 and 80:1. Their musical sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: miktam: a kind of psalm whose meaning is unknown
decisions.reason: As in 16:1. The word heads Psalms 16 and 56-60; its meaning is lost.

decisions.choice: to teach: to be learned and passed on
decisions.reason: The psalm was to be taught, perhaps as David taught the lament over Saul and Jonathan to the people (2 Samuel 1:18).

decisions.choice: To the tune "Lily of the Covenant"; A song
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the terms (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: "shushani edothi" kept as a name at L and B; at Readable the tune "Yungiyungi wa Agano" (Lily of the Covenant)
alternatives: translating "the lily of the testimony" at every level
decisions.reason: The words mean "lily of the testimony", probably naming a tune; Swahili follows the English levels, as with "shoshanimu" in Psalm 45.

decisions.choice: sobre susán edut (L, B); Con la melodía «El lirio del pacto» (R)
decisions.reason: The words seem to mean "on the lily of the testimony", probably a tune. Literal and Balanced keep them as a name in Spanish spelling, as the English keeps them; Readable gives the tune name the English Readable gives.

source.text: בְּהַצּוֹת֨וֹ׀אֶ֥ת אֲרַ֣ם נַהֲרַיִם֮ וְאֶת־אֲרַ֪ם צ֫וֹבָ֥ה וַיָּ֤שָׁב יוֹאָ֗ב וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־אֱד֣וֹם בְּגֵיא־מֶ֑לַח שְׁנֵ֖ים עָשָׂ֣ר אָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: when he fought with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck Edom in [the] Valley of Salt, twelve thousand.

en.L: when he fought with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck Edom in the Valley of Salt, twelve thousand.
en.B: when he fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab came back and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.
en.R: This was when David fought against the Arameans of northern Mesopotamia and of Zobah, and Joab came back and killed twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

fr.L: quand il combattit contre Aram-Naharaïm et contre Aram-Soba, et que Joab revint et frappa Édom dans la vallée du Sel, douze mille [hommes].
fr.B: quand il combattit contre Aram-Naharaïm et Aram-Soba, et que Joab, à son retour, abattit douze mille Édomites dans la vallée du Sel.
fr.R: C’était au moment où David a combattu contre les Araméens du nord de la Mésopotamie et ceux de Soba, et où Joab, à son retour, a tué douze mille Édomites dans la vallée du Sel.

sw.L: alipopigana na Aramu-naharaimu na Aramu-soba, naye Yoabu akarudi akawapiga Edomu katika Bonde la Chumvi, elfu kumi na mbili.
sw.B: alipopigana dhidi ya Aramu-naharaimu na Aramu-soba, naye Yoabu akarudi akawaua watu elfu kumi na mbili wa Edomu katika Bonde la Chumvi.
sw.R: Hii ilikuwa wakati Daudi alipopigana na Waaramu wa kaskazini mwa Mesopotamia na wa Soba, naye Yoabu akarudi akawaua Waedomu elfu kumi na mbili katika Bonde la Chumvi.

es.L: cuando luchó contra Aram-naharaim y contra Aram de Soba, y Joab volvió e hirió a Edom en el valle de la Sal, doce mil.
es.B: cuando luchó contra Aram-naharaim y Aram de Soba, y Joab regresó y abatió a doce mil de Edom en el valle de la Sal.
es.R: Fue cuando David luchó contra los arameos del norte de Mesopotamia y de Soba, y Joab regresó y mató a doce mil edomitas en el valle de la Sal.

decisions.choice: The title is verses 1-2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew counts this long title as two verses, so the verse numbers here are two higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: David's wars with Aram and Edom
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:3-14 and 1 Chronicles 18:3-13 tell of David's victories over the Arameans of Zobah and the Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Those accounts give eighteen thousand and credit David and Abishai; the title gives twelve thousand and names Joab. The psalm itself speaks of a defeat (verses 3-5), perhaps a setback before the victory.

decisions.choice: Aram-naharaim, Aram-zobah: Aramean kingdoms
decisions.reason: Aram-naharaim is "Aram of the two rivers", northern Mesopotamia (Genesis 24:10); Zobah was an Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. The Valley of Salt was probably near the Dead Sea, toward Edom.

decisions.choice: This was when David
decisions.reason: Readable makes the second part of the title its own sentence and names David.

source.text: אֱ֭לֹהִים זְנַחְתָּ֣נוּ פְרַצְתָּ֑נוּ אָ֝נַ֗פְתָּ תְּשׁ֣וֹבֵ֥ב לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: God, you have rejected us; you have broken out on us; you have been angry; you will restore to us.

en.L: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rejected us; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have broken out on us; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been angry; restore us.
en.B: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have thrown us off and burst through our walls. \q You have been angry; turn to us again!
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from us. You have broken down our defenses. \q You have been angry with us. Now come back to us!

fr.L: Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as rejetés ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait brèche parmi nous ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as été en colère ; rétablis-nous.
fr.B: Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as repoussés et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as enfoncé nos murailles. \q Tu as été en colère ; reviens vers nous !
fr.R: Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}es détourné de nous. Tu as brisé nos défenses. \q Tu as été en colère contre nous. Maintenant, reviens vers nous !

sw.L: Ee Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetukataa; {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetuvunja; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umekasirika; uturudishe.
sw.B: Ee Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetutupa na kubomoa kuta zetu. \q Umekasirika; utugeukie tena!
sw.R: Ee Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetuacha. Umebomoa ngome zetu. \q Umetukasirikia. Sasa urudi kwetu!

es.L: Oh Dios, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos has rechazado; {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has irrumpido contra nosotros; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} has airado; restáuranos.
es.B: Dios, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos has desechado y has derribado nuestros muros. \q Te has enojado; ¡vuélvete otra vez a nosotros!
es.R: Dios, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} has alejado de nosotros. Has derribado nuestras defensas. \q Te has enojado con nosotros. ¡Ahora vuelve a nosotros!

decisions.choice: broken out on us: broken through like a breach in a wall
decisions.reason: The verb (parats) is used of breaking through a wall (80:13; 2 Samuel 5:20). The defeat is pictured as God himself breaking through Israel's defenses.

decisions.choice: restore us: a plea
decisions.reason: The verb is in a form that can be a statement, but after the complaint it is a prayer: turn back to us, bring us back to what we were.

decisions.choice: a lament after defeat
decisions.reason: The psalm is a community lament after a defeat (compare 44:10). The title links it to David's wars; verse 12 says God did not go out with Israel's armies.

source.text: הִרְעַ֣שְׁתָּה אֶ֣רֶץ פְּצַמְתָּ֑הּ רְפָ֖ה שְׁבָרֶ֣יהָ כִי־מָֽטָה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have made [the] land quake; you have split it open; repair its fractures, for it is shaking.

en.L: You have made [the] land quake; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have split it open; \q heal its breaches, for it totters.
en.B: You made the land shudder and tore it apart; \q mend its cracks, for it is giving way.
en.R: You have shaken the land as if by an earthquake and split it open. \q Repair its cracks, because it is falling apart.

fr.L: Tu as fait trembler [la] terre ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as fendue ; \q guéris ses brèches, car elle chancelle.
fr.B: Tu as fait frémir le pays et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as déchiré ; \q répare ses fissures, car il s’effondre.
fr.R: Tu as secoué le pays comme par un tremblement de terre et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as fendu. \q Répare ses fissures, parce qu’il tombe en morceaux.

sw.L: Umeitetemesha nchi; {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeipasua; \q uyaponye mavunjiko yake, kwa maana inayumba.
sw.B: Uliifanya nchi itetemeke na kuirarua; \q ziba nyufa zake, kwa maana inaporomoka.
sw.R: Umeitikisa nchi kama kwa tetemeko la ardhi na kuipasua. \q Ziba nyufa zake, kwa sababu inaanguka.

es.L: Has hecho temblar [la] tierra; {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} la has partido; \q sana sus grietas, porque se tambalea.
es.B: Hiciste estremecer la tierra y la desgarraste; \q repara sus grietas, porque se está desmoronando.
es.R: Has sacudido la tierra como con un terremoto y la has partido. \q Repara sus grietas, porque se está cayendo a pedazos.

decisions.choice: the land quaking: defeat pictured as an earthquake
decisions.reason: The shaking of the land is a picture of the nation's collapse after defeat, as if God had sent an earthquake.

decisions.choice: heal: repair
decisions.reason: The verb (rapa') is used for healing a body, and also for repairing what is broken (1 Kings 18:30).

source.text: הִרְאִ֣יתָה עַמְּךָ֣ קָשָׁ֑ה הִ֝שְׁקִיתָ֗נוּ יַ֣יִן תַּרְעֵלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have made your people see a hard [thing]; you have made us drink wine of staggering.

en.L: You have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people see hardship; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made us drink wine of staggering.
en.B: You let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people see hard things; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made us drink a wine that sent us reeling.
en.R: You have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people suffer hard times. \q It is as if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave us strong wine, and now we stagger like drunk people.

fr.L: Tu as fait voir à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple la dureté ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as fait boire un vin de vertige.
fr.B: Tu as fait connaître à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple des choses dures ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as fait boire un vin qui nous fait tituber.
fr.R: Tu as fait passer {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple par des temps difficiles. \q C’est comme si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous avais donné un vin fort, et maintenant nous titubons comme des gens ivres.

sw.L: Umewaonyesha watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} taabu; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetunywesha divai ya kuyumbisha.
sw.B: Umewaacha watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} waone mambo magumu; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetunywesha divai iliyotufanya tuyumbe.
sw.R: Umewafanya watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wapate nyakati ngumu. \q Ni kana kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulitupa divai kali, na sasa tunayumbayumba kama walevi.

es.L: Has hecho ver a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo dureza; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos has hecho beber vino de aturdimiento.
es.B: Dejaste que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo viera cosas duras; \q {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos diste a beber un vino que nos hizo tambalear.
es.R: Has hecho sufrir tiempos duros a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo. \q Es como si {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos hubieras dado vino fuerte, y ahora nos tambaleamos como borrachos.

decisions.choice: wine of staggering: the cup of God's anger
decisions.reason: God's judgment is often pictured as a cup of wine that makes people reel (75:9; Isaiah 51:17). Israel is dazed and helpless.

decisions.choice: It is as if ... like drunk people
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture clear (m1).

source.text: נָ֘תַ֤תָּה לִּירֵאֶ֣יךָ נֵּ֭ס לְהִתְנוֹסֵ֑ס מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י קֹ֣שֶׁט סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have given to those fearing you a banner, to flee because of [the] bow. Selah.

en.L: You have given to those who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a banner, to flee [to it] \q from before the bow. Selah
en.B: For those who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have raised a banner to rally to, \q out of reach of the bow. Selah
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have raised a flag for those who honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, so they can gather around it \q and escape the enemy's arrows. Selah

fr.L: Tu as donné à ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} craignent une bannière, pour fuir [vers elle] \q loin de l’arc. Sélah
fr.B: Pour ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} craignent, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dressé une bannière où se rallier, \q hors de portée de l’arc. Sélah
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as levé un drapeau pour ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}honorent, pour qu’ils se rassemblent autour de lui \q et échappent aux flèches de l’ennemi. Sélah

sw.L: Umewapa wanaokucha {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} bendera, ili wakimbilie [kwake] \q kutoka mbele ya upinde. Sela
sw.B: Kwa ajili ya wanaokucha {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeinua bendera ya kukusanyikia, \q mbali na mishale ya upinde. Sela
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeinua bendera kwa ajili ya wanaokuheshimu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, ili wakusanyike kuizunguka \q na kuepuka mishale ya adui. Sela

es.L: Has dado a los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} temen una bandera, para huir [a ella] \q de delante del arco. Selah
es.B: Para los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} temen, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has alzado una bandera a la cual acudir, \q fuera del alcance del arco. Selah
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has levantado una bandera para los que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} honran, para que se reúnan junto a ella \q y escapen de las flechas del enemigo. Selah

decisions.choice: a banner: a flag to gather around
decisions.reason: The word (nes) is a pole or flag raised as a signal, where an army gathers (Exodus 17:15; Isaiah 5:26).

decisions.choice: to flee from before the bow
alternatives: to be raised because of the truth
decisions.reason: The verb may mean to flee to safety or to rally; the last word is the ordinary word for a bow. Some read it as a rare word for "truth" (Proverbs 22:21), "a banner to be raised for the sake of truth". The line may also be bitter: the banner was a signal to retreat. The sense chosen here goes with the prayer of verse 7.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Readable marks the turn from complaint to God's help, as the meaning chosen in m2 implies.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּן יְדִידֶ֑יךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וַעֲנֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: So that they may be rescued, your beloved ones, save [with] your right hand, and answer me.

en.L: So that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} beloved ones may be rescued, \q save [with] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand, and answer me.
en.B: So that those {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love may be set free, \q bring rescue with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand and answer me!
en.R: Rescue the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love! \q Save us with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power, and answer my prayer!

fr.L: Afin que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} bien-aimés soient délivrés, \q sauve [par] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} droite, et réponds-moi.
fr.B: Pour que ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} aimes soient libérés, \q sauve-les de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main droite et réponds-moi !
fr.R: Sauve les gens que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} aimes ! \q Sauve-nous par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance, et réponds à ma prière !

sw.L: Ili wapendwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} waokolewe, \q uokoe [kwa] mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume, na unijibu.
sw.B: Ili wale {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaowapenda wawekwe huru, \q lete wokovu kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa kuume na unijibu!
sw.R: Uwaokoe watu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaowapenda! \q Utuokoe kwa uweza {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mkuu, na ujibu sala yangu!

es.L: Para que sean librados {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} amados, \q salva [con] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} diestra, y respóndeme.
es.B: Para que los que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} amas sean puestos en libertad, \q trae rescate con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} diestra y ¡respóndeme!
es.R: ¡Rescata al pueblo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} amas! \q Sálvanos con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gran poder, ¡y responde a mi oración!

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: answer me: the word as read
decisions.reason: The words follow the form the Hebrew text's notes say to read, "answer me"; the written form is "answer us", which Psalm 108:7 also reads as "me". The difference is small: the speaker prays for the people.

decisions.choice: right hand: God's power to act
decisions.reason: The right hand is the hand of strength (17:7; 20:7).

decisions.choice: with your great power
decisions.reason: Readable says what the right hand stands for (m3).

decisions.choice: us
decisions.reason: Readable names who is to be saved, the people of the first line.

source.text: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀דִּבֶּ֥ר בְּקָדְשׁ֗וֹ אֶ֫עְלֹ֥זָה אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה שְׁכֶ֑ם וְעֵ֖מֶק סֻכּ֣וֹת אֲמַדֵּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: God has spoken in his holiness: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and [the] Valley of Succoth I will measure off.

en.L: God has spoken in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness: "I will exult; \q I will divide Shechem, \q and the Valley of Succoth I will measure off.
en.B: God has spoken from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place: "I will rejoice \q as I share out Shechem \q and mark off the Valley of Succoth.
en.R: God has spoken from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place. \q He said, "I have won, and I am glad! \q I will divide up the land of Shechem and the Valley of Succoth for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

fr.L: Dieu a parlé dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainteté : « J’exulterai ; \q je partagerai Sichem, \q et la vallée de Souccoth, je la mesurerai.
fr.B: Dieu a parlé depuis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint : « Je me réjouirai \q en distribuant Sichem \q et en mesurant la vallée de Souccoth.
fr.R: Dieu a parlé depuis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint. \q Il a dit : « J’ai gagné, et je suis heureux ! \q Je partagerai la région de Sichem et la vallée de Souccoth pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple.

sw.L: Mungu amenena katika utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: "Nitashangilia; \q nitaigawa Shekemu, \q na Bonde la Sukothi nitalipima.
sw.B: Mungu amesema kutoka mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu: "Nitafurahi \q ninapoigawa Shekemu \q na kulipima Bonde la Sukothi.
sw.R: Mungu amesema kutoka mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu. \q Alisema, "Nimeshinda, nami nimefurahi! \q Nitaigawanya nchi ya Shekemu na Bonde la Sukothi kwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

es.L: Dios ha hablado en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad: «Me regocijaré; \q repartiré Siquem, \q y el valle de Sucot mediré.
es.B: Dios ha hablado desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo: «Me alegraré \q al repartir Siquem \q y al medir el valle de Sucot.
es.R: Dios ha hablado desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo. \q Dijo: «¡He vencido, y estoy feliz! \q Repartiré la tierra de Siquem y el valle de Sucot para {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo.

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: in his holiness: from his holy place, or by his holy nature
decisions.reason: The word (qodesh) can mean holiness or the holy place. God speaks either from his sanctuary or by his holiness, as an oath (89:36).

decisions.choice: Shechem and Succoth: the land given out
decisions.reason: Shechem lay west of the Jordan and Succoth east of it (Genesis 33:17-18). God speaks as a victorious warrior dividing land among his people; the whole land on both sides of the river is his to give.

decisions.choice: God's words
decisions.reason: God's speech runs from here to the end of verse 10.

decisions.choice: He said; I have won; for my people
decisions.reason: Readable makes the start of God's words and the purpose of dividing the land clear (m2).

source.text: לִ֤י גִלְעָ֨ד׀וְלִ֬י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה וְ֭אֶפְרַיִם מָע֣וֹז רֹאשִׁ֑י יְ֝הוּדָ֗ה מְחֹֽקְקִי׃

records.literal_gloss: To me [belongs] Gilead and to me Manasseh, and Ephraim [is the] protection of my head; Judah [is] my commander's staff.

en.L: Gilead [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and Manasseh [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; \q and Ephraim [is] the helmet of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head; \q Judah [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} scepter.
en.B: Gilead belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Manasseh is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; \q Ephraim is the helmet on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head, \q Judah the staff of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rule.
en.R: Gilead and Manasseh belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Ephraim is like a helmet that protects {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head. \q Judah is the rod I rule with.

fr.L: Galaad [est] à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et Manassé [est] à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q et Éphraïm [est] le casque de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} tête ; \q Juda [est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sceptre.
fr.B: Galaad {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient, Manassé est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q Éphraïm est le casque sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} tête, \q Juda le bâton de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} commandement.
fr.R: Galaad et Manassé {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiennent. \q Éphraïm est comme un casque qui protège {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} tête. \q Juda est le bâton avec lequel je règne.

sw.L: Gileadi [ni] {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, na Manase [ni] {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; \q na Efraimu [ni] kofia ya chuma ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}; \q Yuda [ni] fimbo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ya enzi.
sw.B: Gileadi ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Manase ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; \q Efraimu ni kofia ya chuma kichwani {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}, \q Yuda ni fimbo ya utawala {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.R: Gileadi na Manase ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Efraimu ni kama kofia ya chuma inayokilinda kichwa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}. \q Yuda ni fimbo ninayotawala nayo.

es.L: Galaad [es] {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, y Manasés [es] {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}; \q y Efraín [es] el casco de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cabeza; \q Judá [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cetro.
es.B: Galaad {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece, Manasés es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}; \q Efraín es el casco de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cabeza, \q Judá el bastón de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mando.
es.R: Galaad y Manasés {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenecen. \q Efraín es como un casco que protege {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cabeza. \q Judá es la vara con la que gobierno.

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah: Israel's own tribes
decisions.reason: Gilead lay east of the Jordan, and Manasseh lived on both sides of it. Ephraim was the strongest tribe in the north, Judah the royal tribe in the south. God claims them all as his own.

decisions.choice: my scepter: the staff of the ruler
decisions.reason: The word (mechoqeq) is the ruler's staff, as in Jacob's blessing of Judah: "the scepter will not depart from Judah" (Genesis 49:10).

decisions.choice: the protection of my head: a helmet
decisions.reason: The phrase means a stronghold for the head, that is, a helmet.

source.text: מוֹאָ֤ב׀סִ֬יר רַחְצִ֗י עַל־אֱ֭דוֹם אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ נַעֲלִ֑י עָ֝לַ֗י פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת הִתְרֹעָֽעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Moab [is the] pot of my washing; over Edom I throw my sandal; over me, Philistia, shout aloud.

en.L: Moab [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} washbasin; \q over Edom I throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sandal; \q over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Philistia, shout aloud."
en.B: Moab is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} washing bowl; \q on Edom I toss {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sandal; \q Philistia, raise your shout to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}!"
en.R: Moab is only a bowl I wash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet in. \q I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sandal on Edom to show it is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. \q Philistia, shout because I have won!"

fr.L: Moab [est] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} bassin pour {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} laver ; \q sur Édom je jette {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sandale ; \q à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, Philistie, pousse des cris. »
fr.B: Moab est la cuvette où je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lave ; \q sur Édom je lance {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sandale ; \q Philistie, pousse vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} tes cris ! »
fr.R: Moab n’est qu’une cuvette où je lave {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} pieds. \q Je jetterai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sandale sur Édom pour montrer qu’il est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Philistie, pousse des cris, car j’ai gagné ! »

sw.L: Moabu [ni] bakuli {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la kunawia; \q juu ya Edomu nitatupa kiatu {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}; \q juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Ee Ufilisti, piga kelele."
sw.B: Moabu ni bakuli {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la kunawia; \q juu ya Edomu ninatupa kiatu {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}; \q Ee Ufilisti, nipigie {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kelele za shangwe!"
sw.R: Moabu ni bakuli tu la kunawia miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Nitatupa kiatu {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} juu ya Edomu kuonyesha kwamba ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Ee Ufilisti, piga kelele kwa sababu nimeshinda!"

es.L: Moab [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vasija para lavarme; \q sobre Edom echo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sandalia; \q ¡sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Filistea, grita!».
es.B: Moab es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palangana; \q sobre Edom arrojo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sandalia; \q ¡Filistea, lanza tu grito ante {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}!».
es.R: Moab no es más que una vasija donde {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lavo los pies. \q Echaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sandalia sobre Edom para mostrar que es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}. \q ¡Filistea, grita porque he vencido!».

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: my washbasin: the lowest servant's task
decisions.reason: Moab will be like a basin for washing the feet, a humble household object. The proud neighbor becomes God's servant.

decisions.choice: throw my sandal: claim as one's own
decisions.reason: Throwing or setting down a sandal on land was a way of claiming it (Ruth 4:7; compare Deuteronomy 25:9).

decisions.choice: over me, Philistia, shout: Philistia must hail the victor
alternatives: over Philistia I shout in triumph (Psalm 108:10)
Philistia, shout against me if you dare
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tells Philistia to shout "over me" or "because of me", most likely the shout of a defeated people greeting their conqueror. Psalm 108:10 has instead "over Philistia I shout in triumph".

decisions.choice: to show it is mine; because I have won
decisions.reason: Readable explains the pictures (m2, m3, m4).

source.text: מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי עִ֣יר מָצ֑וֹר מִ֖י נָחַ֣נִי עַד־אֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will bring me [to the] city of fortification? Who has led me to Edom?

en.L: Who will bring me [to the] fortified city? \q Who has led me to Edom?
en.B: Who will take me into the walled city? \q Who will guide me all the way to Edom?
en.R: Who will lead me into the strong city of Edom? \q Who will take me there?

fr.L: Qui me conduira [dans la] ville fortifiée ? \q Qui m’a mené jusqu’en Édom ?
fr.B: Qui me fera entrer dans la ville fortifiée ? \q Qui me guidera jusqu’en Édom ?
fr.R: Qui me conduira dans la ville forte d’Édom ? \q Qui m’y emmènera ?

sw.L: Nani ataniingiza [katika] mji wa ngome? \q Nani ameniongoza mpaka Edomu?
sw.B: Nani atanipeleka ndani ya mji wenye kuta? \q Nani ataniongoza njia yote mpaka Edomu?
sw.R: Nani ataniongoza kuingia katika mji imara wa Edomu? \q Nani atanipeleka huko?

es.L: ¿Quién me llevará [a la] ciudad fortificada? \q ¿Quién me ha guiado hasta Edom?
es.B: ¿Quién me hará entrar en la ciudad amurallada? \q ¿Quién me guiará hasta Edom?
es.R: ¿Quién me llevará a la ciudad fuerte de Edom? \q ¿Quién me guiará hasta allá?

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: the fortified city: Edom's stronghold
decisions.reason: Probably Bozrah or Sela, the rock city of Edom (2 Kings 14:7), hard to take by force.

decisions.choice: the king speaks
decisions.reason: After God's words the speaker is the king or the people. The past tense "has led me" asks who has ever brought anyone there: only God could.

decisions.choice: has led me: who could lead me
decisions.reason: The verb is past in form; the question is the same as the first, and Psalm 108:11 has the same form.

source.text: הֲלֹֽא־אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ וְֽלֹא־תֵצֵ֥א אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] not you, God, [who] have rejected us? And not you go out, God, with our armies.

en.L: [Is it] not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God, [who] have rejected us? \q And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not go out, God, with our armies.
en.B: Is it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God, who rejected us \q and no longer march out with our armies?
en.R: God, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can lead us, even though {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from us. \q You no longer go with our armies into battle.

fr.L: N’[est-ce] pas {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Dieu, [qui] nous as rejetés ? \q Et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne sors pas, Dieu, avec nos armées.
fr.B: N’est-ce pas {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Dieu, qui nous as rejetés \q et qui ne sors plus avec nos armées ?
fr.R: Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} seul peux nous conduire, même si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}es détourné de nous. \q Tu ne vas plus avec nos armées au combat.

sw.L: [Je], si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee Mungu, [uliyetukataa]? \q Wala {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hutoki, Ee Mungu, pamoja na majeshi yetu.
sw.B: Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee Mungu, uliyetukataa \q na kuacha kutoka pamoja na majeshi yetu?
sw.R: Ee Mungu, ni {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} peke {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} unayeweza kutuongoza, ingawa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umetuacha. \q Hutoki tena pamoja na majeshi yetu kwenda vitani.

es.L: ¿No [eres] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, oh Dios, [quien] nos ha rechazado? \q Y no sales, oh Dios, con nuestros ejércitos.
es.B: ¿No eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Dios, quien nos rechazó \q y ya no sales con nuestros ejércitos?
es.R: Dios, solo {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} puedes guiarnos, aunque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} has alejado de nosotros. \q Ya no sales con nuestros ejércitos a la batalla.

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: Is it not you? the answer to verse 11
decisions.reason: The question answers verse 11: the only one who can lead the king to Edom is God, the very God who has rejected his people (verse 3).

decisions.choice: go out with our armies: lead them in battle
decisions.reason: God went out before Israel's armies (Judges 4:14; 2 Samuel 5:24). His absence meant defeat (44:10).

decisions.choice: only you can lead us
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the answer the question implies (m2).

decisions.choice: leaving out the second "God"
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the address once; Literal keeps both.

source.text: הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ עֶזְרָ֣ת מִצָּ֑ר וְ֝שָׁ֗וְא תְּשׁוּעַ֥ת אָדָם׃

records.literal_gloss: Give to us help from [the] foe, and worthless [is the] salvation of humankind.

en.L: Give us help against [the] foe, \q for worthless [is] the salvation of humankind.
en.B: Help us against the enemy, \q for any rescue that people can bring is useless.
en.R: Help us fight the enemy. \q No human being can save us.

fr.L: Donne-nous du secours contre [l’]adversaire, \q car vain [est] le salut {{gender:de l’humain|de l’homme}}.
fr.B: Viens à notre aide contre l’ennemi, \q car tout secours venu des humains est inutile.
fr.R: Aide-nous à combattre l’ennemi. \q Aucun être humain ne peut nous sauver.

sw.L: Utupe msaada dhidi ya mtesi, \q kwa maana wokovu wa mwanadamu [ni] bure.
sw.B: Utusaidie dhidi ya adui, \q kwa maana msaada wowote wa wanadamu hauna maana.
sw.R: Utusaidie kupigana na adui. \q Hakuna binadamu anayeweza kutuokoa.

es.L: Danos ayuda contra [el] adversario, \q porque vana [es] la salvación del ser humano.
es.B: Ayúdanos contra el enemigo, \q porque de nada sirve el rescate que puede dar la gente.
es.R: Ayúdanos a pelear contra el enemigo. \q Ningún ser humano nos puede salvar.

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: worthless: empty, in vain
decisions.reason: The word (shav') means emptiness; human help cannot save (33:16-17; 146:3).

decisions.choice: and: for
decisions.reason: The "and" gives the reason for the plea.

records.literal_gloss: In God we will do strength, and he will tread down our foes.

en.L: In God we will do valiantly, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will tread down our foes.
en.B: With God on our side we will fight with courage; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who will crush our foes underfoot.
en.R: With God's help we will fight bravely. \q He will trample our enemies.

fr.L: En Dieu nous ferons des exploits, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} écrasera nos adversaires.
fr.B: Avec Dieu à nos côtés, nous combattrons avec courage ; \q c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui piétinera nos adversaires.
fr.R: Avec l’aide de Dieu, nous combattrons courageusement. \q Il piétinera nos ennemis.

sw.L: Katika Mungu tutafanya kwa ushujaa, \q na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawakanyaga watesi wetu.
sw.B: Mungu akiwa upande wetu tutapigana kwa ujasiri; \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye atakayewaponda adui zetu chini ya miguu.
sw.R: Kwa msaada wa Mungu tutapigana kwa ushujaa. \q Atawakanyaga adui zetu.

es.L: En Dios haremos proezas, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pisoteará a nuestros adversarios.
es.B: Con Dios de nuestro lado lucharemos con valor; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es quien aplastará a nuestros enemigos.
es.R: Con la ayuda de Dios pelearemos con valentía. \q Él pisoteará a nuestros enemigos.

decisions.choice: Psalm 108 repeats verses 7-14
decisions.reason: Verses 7-14 of this psalm appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 108:7-14, joined there to 57:8-12.

decisions.choice: do strength: act with courage and win
decisions.reason: The phrase ("do strength") means to act bravely and with success (118:15-16; Numbers 24:18).

decisions.choice: he: God himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: God, not the army, will win the victory.
